If participants learn a repeating state-action graph with directionally valenced numerical operations, then the entorhinal-hippocampal system will represent states according to their action affordances and horizontal gaze will lateralize during memory retrieval in line with positive versus negative action valences, because the brain constructs cognitive maps of abstract action spaces by repurposing spatial coding mechanisms to organize relational state-action knowledge.
